The death toll rose to three today in the collapse of a building under construction near the Philippine capital, with 17 people still believed missing, authorities said.

Two workers pinned beneath the wreckage were found alive after the nine-storey structure gave way yesterday, hitting a nearby hotel and killing a Malaysian guest.

But the two workers trapped at the site in Angeles, which is north of the capital Manila, died despite rescue efforts.

“The first of the two was pulled out alive, but unfortunately, his body gave out and he did not survive. Doctors could not resuscitate him,” regional fire bureau spokeswoman Maria Leah Sajili told AFP.

Subject: Urgent Appeal: Halt Tree Cutting Along Quirino Avenue and Other Areas in Manila for the SALEX Project

Dear Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna,

We are writing to you as concerned citizens of Manila regarding the ongoing mass cutting of mature trees along Quirino Avenue to make way for the Southern Access Link Expressway (SALEX) project.  

While we recognize the importance of infrastructure development for alleviating traffic congestion and supporting economic growth, the removal of hundreds of decades-old trees including large canopy trees and species like narra represents a significant and irreversible loss to Manila’s already limited urban greenery.   

These trees provide essential shade, improve air quality, reduce urban heat, support biodiversity, and offer psychological and environmental benefits to communities in a densely populated city.  

We respectfully urge the DENR to:  

- Immediately review and consider suspending further tree-cutting permits for the SALEX project in affected areas.  

- Prioritize maximum earth-balling and transplantation of remaining mature trees wherever technically feasible, rather than cutting.  

- Enforce stricter compensatory planting requirements that go beyond seedlings, including the protection and maintenance of replacement trees to ensure long-term survival.  

- Conduct a more comprehensive environmental impact reassessment that fully weighs the long-term ecological costs against the project’s benefits, with greater public consultation.   

Manila needs both better infrastructure and a healthier, greener environment.   

Destroying established urban forests should be a last resort, not the default approach.  

We hope your leadership at the DENR will champion a more balanced and sustainable path that protects our remaining trees while pursuing progress.   

Your intervention on this matter would be greatly appreciated by many residents who value Manila’s livability.  

Thank you for your time and attention to this urgent environmental concern.  

Sincerely,  

Citizens of Manila

LOOK: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. leads the inspection of the Sunog Apog Pumping Station in Tondo, Manila, on May 25, as the government moves to restore the facility’s operations after six years of inactivity. The President orders the pumping station to be fully operational by June to help mitigate the recurring flooding experienced by residents during the rainy season and typhoons.

Three of the four heavy-duty electromechanical pumps are now operational, while the fourth is expected to be activated by June. Marcos also directs the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to conduct regular cleaning and maintenance of pumping stations to prevent clogging caused by garbage.

Joining the President during the inspection are DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon, Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso, MMDA Chairman Romando Artes, and MMDA General Manager Nicolas Torre. 

📷: Mark Balmores | MB
